item.content:encoded:
I'm sincerely curious about the original, and think it could have survived at least in the article's history. But that aside, nothing to complain. Old articles are interesting for several reasons, but I don't think they should be sacred. This site existed for a number of years, now, but not that much, and most of the silly articles of the time were already silly back them, it is just that they were read just by the same group of teenagers.

+ I have some praise to do
- Because it have to be said

This current version is a strong article by itself. It isn't an easy subject and certainly won't appeal to everyone. I do have a lot of mixed feelings myself, and can't say I upvoted without a doubt. But the more I think about it, the more I feel the skip as a live character, the distinct reactions it get coming from real people. It isn't a deep story, but it does convince that there is dept to what is going on.

And as much as not every character in it is respectful of what is happening, I do think the author was respectful enough. Not every line is of my liking, but again, it isn't an easy subject. This won't be my favorite skip, or even get near it, but it is something worth keeping in the site.

+ And I have issues to point out
- Because that's my way of improving things

Some comments and critiques about specific points.

Containment Procedures; Paragraph 1:
I think just describing the electrical floor should be enough. Since it is a Containment chamber and in the Special Containment section, just saying Humanoid Containment Chamber says the rest. In particular, since the tests and behaviors described later make it seems like it won't use any of the furnishings described, they have no point in being described. It could get some more complex behavior, though.

Containment Procedures; Paragraph 2:
Instead of previously stating that the chamber have a safe spot (that the skip could learn to exploit), the staff here could be described with apparel to safely contact the electrified floor, like the things the very workers who installed the wiring probably used. This isn't so hard to get, since a lot of high-voltage cables can't be safely turned off for maintenance.

Description; Initial:
I feel a lack of chemical analysis of the material. The description given is only about its texture, but since it chips easily and the skip shatters itself, there is nothing preventing sampling.

Description; Pattern Z:
Pattern Z could have a little more to it, even to justify the furnishing. Not a lot more, I think I got the point on it moving so little, but a little more. Maybe it moves once or twice daily, for a few minutes. Interact with some furnishing, even if simply to try a new pose in front of the mirror, be it sexier or shier, or whatever.

Description; Pattern Y:
It could have observations about long exposures. Even if it doesn't change at all in behavior, it would be worth of note how it evolves through at least a day or two to constant exposure to a male subject.

Description; Pattern X:
The section about intervening obstacles should be eliminated or elaborated upon. Does it need to be able to perceive through magical senses? If yes, how the Foundation tried to determine the limits of those senses? How it does behave while there is an obstacle? Even if the end result is still the same, it is missing the attempts from the Foundation to evaluate and achieve such conclusion.

Description; Missing Patterns:
As much as it isn't the focus, a brief description on other situations should be done. A simple manner to do so could be saying that non-human presence causes no alteration on the current pattern, and that tests with non-conforming people resulted in mixed behaviors from previous pattern, with details on a non-existent document.

Addendum; A:
It could be added a note on attempts to identify the other mannequins as the victims. True or false, it is too obvious a conclusion for the Foundation to not try. It is relevant, either way.

Addendum; B:
I'm not sure about what was the purpose of the test, what they meant with reducing it's capabilities. It could be clarified.

item.title: Creepy and Charming
item.content:encoded:
This is one of the best I have seen in ages. This will certainly cost me some sleep!! I love it!

This SCP is both interesting, and terrifyingly cold. It endears itself to become the perfect woman. Yet it can not become that and it knows it.

The manner of the SCP in attempting to model itself after the current times by reacting to the words spoken or thoughts about it suggests that it is aware that times change. It remodels itself to fit the desired picture of a woman. It is willing to go to great lengths to achieve its goal as well. This points toward a human like consciousness.

The age of the item in question seems to be unknown, further adding to the mystery of it. How did this SCP gain consciousness though? That is a question that makes it so dangerous. It also actively attacks females or persons identifying as female to further its goal. This is wonderfully crafted. It doesn't just go off genetics, but the mental state of the persons around it.

As well, the bit of history pointing toward persons within the foundation working to cause it to have a breach of security adds further power to the story. To think that someone may see it as a living breathing person makes it seem so much more dangerous.

Definite upvote!!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to agree with MrWrong on his analysis of SCP-166 vs. 847 regarding the misogyny angle. I may have oversold the misogyny of the original 847 in my author post, but I know that many people did have a problem with how 847 was a hot chick thing that attacked women because reasons. 847 is one of the main examples of monster misogyny on the TVTropes page, so yes, although it wasn't the main factor, it was a compounding factor to the article's problems.

However, the main problem of the original 847, as mentioned above, was how unexplored the "hot chick thing that attacked women" angle was. That's what allowed the article to feel more misogynistic in the end. When you ask why, you end up with the answer, "the original author liked it, I guess." That led to all sorts of problematic conclusions like "the author liked women that were things" and "attacking women is attention grabbing and cool" that really brought down the feel of the piece. That's why I said it was naively misogynistic; it wasn't intentional. It's just the reading that came out of it.

Incidentally, for authors who want to explore hot-button issues, this is the real challenge. An insufficiently careful exploration of the theme of the piece just ends up looking like exploitation. I know there are people who don't like what I've done with 847 either. Getting it to this point led me to tons of hand-wringing anyway. The original 847 didn't explore the concept well and ended up failing in the long term.

As for 166, it does deconstruct the succubus and makes it clearer what each part actually means. (Intriguingly, SCP-029 also involves a young naked woman who can bend men to her will, but it doesn't feel nearly as sexy.) But that's the difference between a well-explored and poorly-explored concept. You can write fiction about unchecked female objectification. A good article traces back the source of that objectification to its roots. A poor article ends up assigning the source of that objectification to the author.

I hope I did well. But that's for you to decide.

item.content:encoded:
Drawing on my memory of the previous 847 and SCP-166, there is a huge difference between the two. I find this comparison to be rather flawed.

166 bothers to take apart the concept of the succubus and make her a character. The fetish-esque traits of 166 are depicted in an objective observation of attributes, and does not extol the fetish value of those traits. Also, it ties itself to the story of Clef and sheds more light to the doctor beyond "seriously amoral Foundation doctor".

From my memory of 847, it was formerly a female-shaped mannequin that kills women for reasons unknown. It did not really do anything to the concept it had to work with, which ended up making that one be a sort of monster with a specific target group.

Therefore, the issue here is not misogynism. It is the weakness of not exploring concepts well enough.

item.content:encoded:
I agree this is objectively better than the original, and I applaud the author for his dedication to saving it from the dust bin. He didn't really even change anything, merely added on to what was already there.

I do however regret that a rewrite was necessary, since for me part of series 1's charm is precisely that a lot of the scips from those days no longer meet site standards. As the author pointed out, the original 847 had fanart and youtube readings by multiple individuals. As far as I'm concerned, anything that's been around for years, especially a series 1 scip, and has a decent amount of fandom appreciation deserves to be archived for posterity's sake. I really think the admins should consider expanding the Heritage Collection.

What I really don't understand is why this scip was voted to below zero for being 'naively misogynistic' when 166 still enjoys a score of nearly a hundred. I realize this isn't really the place for an anti-166 rant, but it just really makes no sense to me. She's a hot teenage girl who has to be naked, has to consume semen, and it's literally her fault that every guy and their creepy uncle tries to rape her. Oh, and her father (presumed to be Clef) killed her mother right in front of her when she was little and doesn't think it was that big of a deal. How is none of that worse that the old 847? Personally, I find 166 to be only slightly less disgusting than The Saddest Necrophile.
